note: Plumb --matcher through nestor decision check so a caller with [semantic] installed can point the fuzzy scan at an embedding matcher. Plumbing only; the calibrated bar for the semantic matcher is deferred to a seat that can reach the model host.

decisions.question: Should nestor decision check accept a --matcher argument, so a caller can swap in a semantic scorer for the fuzzy scan without patching Python?
decisions.commitment: Yes. nestor/cli.py cmd_decision now accepts --matcher (default 'string'), routes it through answer.load_matcher(name), and passes the resulting matcher to DecisionMemory(matcher=...). The default is unchanged: no --matcher argument produces exactly the shipped behaviour (StringMatcher at the shipped 0.55 fuzzy bar). A --matcher name that isn't installed or isn't reachable (semantic without [semantic], semantic with an egress-blocked model host) fails at load with the same message the extras' import guards already produce -- there is no silent degradation to string. Gated by tests/test_decision_check_matcher.py (3 tests): the default-is-unchanged baseline, a raw-score stub matcher that proves the fuzzy scan actually calls .score() on the injected matcher (split-verified: reverting the plumbing turns the assertion red with 'fuzzy != none'), and a real semantic-load test that runs only when [semantic] is installed AND the model host is reachable.
decisions.why: Decision 0154's doors_closed clause explicitly names semantic embeddings as the tail fix for the ~25% of decisions with too little character overlap; decision 0192 measured that a lexical stem-strip does NOT close that gap. The seam DecisionMemory already had a matcher parameter -- it was just not reachable from the CLI, so a caller had to write Python to try semantic on their decision store. Adding --matcher makes the extra actually useful without changing what the shipped default does.

decisions.question: What is the calibrated bar for --matcher semantic on the decision domain, and what is its wrong-key rate?
decisions.commitment: Deferred. This seat's egress proxy blocks fastembed's model download from HuggingFace (httpx.ProxyError: 403 Forbidden on a `nestor decision check --matcher semantic` end-to-end run this session), so the calibration cannot be measured here. The commitment is that the calibration ships as a separate PR from a seat where the model can download, updating docs/decision-rewording-bench.md with the semantic column and this decision's second question with the measured numbers. Until then, a caller running --matcher semantic against the dogfood corpus uses the string-matcher default bar (0.55), which is measured for StringMatcher, NOT for the semantic backend -- and that mismatch is noted in the --help text so nobody trusts a semantic serve on a bar tuned for a different scorer.
decisions.why: The seat rule 'say what you read, not what you concluded' applies to numbers as strictly as to prose. Naming a calibrated semantic bar without having measured it would put a number in the record that any future run could refute -- exactly what the covenant refuses. Bench/bench_decision_n1.py's --sweep mode plus the arc-questions probe are the shape the follow-up PR will use; both need network access this seat does not have.

decisions.question: Should the default matcher on the decision domain change from string to semantic?
decisions.commitment: Not in this PR. Changing the default would silently move every seat's decision-check behaviour, and the calibration for the new bar is not yet measured. A default change is a separate decision with its own rewording-bench numbers attached -- proposed after the follow-up measurement PR lands, if the numbers support it.
decisions.why: docs/decision-rewording-bench.md's key finding is 'calibrate per corpus, not one number for all'. Shipping a default-semantic without measured wrong-key numbers would violate that rule and impose a bar chosen for the CI/lint job on every user's local decision-check run. The plumbing being available at --matcher is enough for anyone who wants to measure it themselves.
